City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
October 1, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:02 p.m. , on October 1, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on September 26, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht
INVOCATION: Mayor Ury
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiation's - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
CS2.
Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission Viejo v. the State of California, Case No. 34 2012 8000 1203.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed item CS1 and provided direction for staff follow-up. For item CS2, the Council gave direction with the understanding that staff will be meeting with State representatives later in the month and more information will follow.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
4th Annual Readers’ Festival
The City Council received the presentation from Director of Library and Cultural Services, Stephanie Tanton.
P2.
Recognize the Lion’s Heart - Teens Giving Back Organization
Mayor Ury presented a Certificate of Appreciation to co-founders Terry and Spencer Corwin and the Lion’s Heart volunteers.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Desi Kiss, M.V.: proposed that Saddleback College become a university as soon as possible and asked the City Council to support his proposal; asked Council Member Schlicht to explain a discrepancy in budget numbers; inquired about secret meetings regarding the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS); and stated that Mayor Ury provided false and misleading statements in his candidate statement.
Bob Hayes, M.V.: provided the City Council Members with information on National Bullying Prevention Month which is held in October.
Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: stated that election signs that he placed in the City have been taken and replaced with different signs, and he asked that the Council notify the Sheriff’s Department and the FBI.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that while he was addressing his comments at the last meeting the Mayor laughed at him and he has seen other examples of disrespect from the dais.
Joe Holtzman, M.V.: announced that the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) will hold a public meeting to discuss San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station issues on October 9, 2012, from 6:00 to 9:30 p.m. at the St. Regis Monarch Beach Hotel. Mr. Holtzman urged everyone to attend the meeting.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: congratulated the City on the awards that were bestowed on Mission Viejo by the Association of California Cities-Orange County. She also announced that the new Oral Histories project is complete and she encouraged residents to visit the City’s web site to see a preview. Lastly, Mrs. Bucknum stated that she is running for City Council to serve the community in a better way.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 2 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
3.
Check Register dated September 7, 2012 in the amount of $2,087,464.60
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated September 14, 2012 in the amount of $434,079.10
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Fourth Quarter of FY 2011-12
Received and filed.
6.
Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Fourth Quarter of 2011-12
Received and filed.
7.
Quarterly Financial Report for the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency - Fourth Quarter of 2011-12
Received and filed.
8.
Semi-Annual Financial Reports for the Community Development Financing Authority - For the Year Ended June 30, 2012
Received and filed.
9.
2012 Speed Limit Update
Adopted Ordinance 12-295 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.
10.
Biennial Update of the City of Mission Viejo’s Conflict of Interest Code
Adopted Resolution 12-60 Amending the City of Mission Viejo Conflict of Interest Code.
11.
Request by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a One-Time Exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City Facilities
Approved the request by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.
12.
Revisions to Flexible Benefit Plan and Fixed Monthly City Contribution Schedule
Adopted Resolution 12-61 Revising the City’s Flexible Benefit Plans and Fixed Monthly City Contribution Schedule effective January 1, 2013.
13.
Marguerite Parkway Civic Core Median Island Landscape Improvements from Estanciero to Via Florecer (CIP 799)
(1) Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids the Marguerite Parkway Median Island Civic Core Enhancement (CIP 799) between Estanciero and Via Florecer; and (2) adopted Resolution 12-62 Approving and Authorizing Program Supplement No. N023 to the Administering Agency-State Agreement No. 1-5451 for Federal-Aid Projects Between the State Department of Transportation and the City of Mission Viejo.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
Mayor Ury
25.
Donation to the Orange County Peace Officers Memorial
Marilyn McDougall, M.V.: representing the Orange County Sheriff’s Department, she discussed the new Orange County Peace Officers Memorial and asked the Council for their support. Mrs. McDougall noted that further information can be found at www.ocpeaceofficersmemorial.com .
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to allocate $7,500 for a donation to the Orange County Peace Officers Memorial.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
14.
Annual Routine Landscape Maintenance - Marguerite Parkway Phase 2 - 2012
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report and answered the City Council Members questions.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to allocate $200,000 for slope renovation of area 1, as outlined in the staff report, and give staff the discretion to determine how much area can be covered with that dollar amount.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Kelley
ABSENT:
None
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
2.
City Council Minutes
Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: referring to item 14 on the last agenda and 9 on this agenda, he stated that the speed limit on Alicia Parkway from Jeronimo to the west city limits should be increased from 45 miles per hour to at least 55 mph.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 17, 2012, as presented.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
ABSTAIN:
Council Member Schlicht.
(Pursuant to City Council Policy, an abstention will be viewed as support for the majority decision.)
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
15.
Community Services Commission Request to Increase Community Services Funding for next fiscal year 2013-2014
Community Services Commissioner Wendy Bucknum outlined the Commission’s request to increase the Community Services funding back to the prior level of $75,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2013-14.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to increase the Community Services funding to $75,000 beginning with fiscal year 2013-14 and direct staff to return with a report for Council to consider increasing the funding in the current fiscal year.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
16.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed OCFA’s Ready Set Go program and questioned the amount of money that is paid to staff who manage the program. He discussed OCFA’s proposed increase in inspection fees and stated that OCFA charged businesses for inspections that were not done.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
17.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
18.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin Hills TCA therefore she had no report.
19.
Association of California Cities - Orange County (ACC-OC) Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
20.
Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board
City Manager Wilberg presented the report.
City Attorney’s Report
City Attorney Bill Curley commended the City Council for refusing to pay the State $2.6 million especially in light of the State’s admission that they were wrong. Referring to item 23 on the agenda, he noted that staff will return with a housekeeping ordinance if the Rule of Law resolution is adopted. The ordinance will not change anything but will memorialize the Council’s decision. Lastly, Mr. Curley noted that the Governor recently approved some pending litigation, none of which present an immediate jeopardy to Mission Viejo.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)
21.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley announced that she has OCFA staff responses to some of the questions that Mr. Wontrobski has asked and she will make those available to the Council as well. She reminded residents to mark their calendars for October 4 and October 10, for two events having to do with prescription drug overdoses in our young people. She noted that Mayor Pro Tem Reardon will share further details about the programs during her comments. Council Member Kelley reminded residents of the Readers’ Festival on Sunday, October 14 from noon to 6:00 p.m. and she stated that it is going to be a fantastic event. She also discussed the annual Walk Against Drugs which will be held this year on October 20. The event begins at Mission Viejo High School at 8:00 a.m. and this year’s keynote speaker is former professional tennis player Peanut Louie Harper who has recently collaborated with John Wooden, on a children’s book entitled Inch and Miles: the Journey to Success. Council Member Kelley announced that there is still space available for youth groups to host fundraising activities at the fair which follows the Walk Against Drugs and more information is available on the police services page of the City’s website. Council Member Kelley mentioned that Hometown Halloween is another fun event and a nice service for the residents. It will be held on October 27 from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. at the Murray Center. She noted that the Community of Character Committee could use additional members and those interested in joining can give her a call. Lastly, Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of October is respect.
Council Member Leckness
22.
"Second Annual Campout with the Mayor" and One-Time Exemption to Municipal Code Chapter 13.04, Sec. 13.04.030(n) Prohibiting Individuals From Being in any Park Overnight
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the date of October 20, 2012, for the "Second Annual Campout with the Mayor," and approve a one-time exemption to Municipal Code Chapter 13.04 Sec. 13.04.030 (n) prohibiting individuals from being in any park overnight.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht announced that there is a Republican Orange County GOP headquarters office at 22195 El Paseo, Suite 190, in Rancho Santa Margarita. They are looking for phone bank volunteers as well as precinct walkers. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote for national bullying prevention month: “It isn’t big to make others feel small.”
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
23.
E-Verify Resolution
Steve Serra, M.V.: outlined the proposed resolution.
Dale Tyler, M.V.: expressed support for the proposed resolution.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt Resolution 12-63 in Support of the Rule of Law and in Support of Electronic Employment Eligibility Verification.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
By consensus, the City Council directed staff to add language to the City’s bid specifications to ask contractors what process they are using to verify a potential employee’s citizenship, for informational purposes only.
24.
Status of Kaleidoscope’s Signage Proposal(s)
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented her report.
The following thanked Mayor Pro Tem Reardon for bringing this matter forward and expressed opposition to electronic billboards: Larry Gilbert, M.V. and Dale Tyler, M.V.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to call the previous question.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon encouraged residents to attend the October 9 oversight status meeting regarding the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station. She noted that the City has delayed its own Town Hall meeting on San Onofre until after Southern California Edison provides its corrective action letter. City Manager Wilberg has asked that Edison’s Senior Vice President, Pete Dietrich, be present at the Town Hall meeting to speak and answer questions. She further announced that she and Mayor Ury have signed letters to the NRC and the CPUC so the City is actively engaged in the issues at SONGS and want the residents to be as informed as possible. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she and Mayor Ury recently visited an Orange County Islamic Foundation event at the mosque in Mission Viejo where they met some very wonderful people. The mosque’s members are very moderate in their approach and very concerned with how they are perceived. They want the community to know that first and foremost, they are American citizens and Mission Viejo residents are invited to attend an open house at the mosque on October 7. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her tour of the new LA Fitness and she discussed upcoming events at the Kaleidoscope center. She also outlined her meeting with CUSD Superintendent Farley regarding the epidemic with accidental drug overdoses in the age group of 15 to 25. She reminded residents that the City will be hosting a screening of the movie Behind the Orange Curtain which follows actual people who have had real experiences with drug overdoses. The Community of Character will host a follow-up event on October 10 to provide parents, adults and teens the opportunity to talk with a panel of experts about the drug overdose problem. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon encouraged residents to get to these important events and she thanked her colleagues for their support.
24.
Status of Kaleidoscope’s Signage Proposal(s) (REVISITED for public comment)
Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: stated that Kaleidoscope will never survive as a retail center and everything is wrong about it. He stated that the Council needs to look into the future before approving retail centers.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury noted that some people have a very strong desire to turn Kaleidoscope signage into a political issue. He finds it suspect that there are anonymous fliers circulating throughout the City suggesting that the Council is going to approve housing on the Casta del Sol golf course and new signage at Kaleidoscope. He stated that neither is going to happen but there are people who don't have much to stand on so they run around saying these things. Mayor Ury concluded his comments by encouraging residents to attend the Walk Against Drugs on October 20.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:57 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, October 15, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of October 15, 2012
